log.notes: mcp/ is data-plane-only: never calls an LLM, never embeds the analysis prompt. Only fetches Jira/Confluence/CSV data via src/sources/*.js unchanged. bin/ripple.js (v1 CLI) confirmed untouched and still works standalone; the MCP server is additive.
Verified (not assumed) that GitHub Copilot CLI and Antigravity CLI support MCP. SKILL.md is Claude-Code-specific and needs a per-host equivalent for hosts without a Skill primitive.

An earlier scaffold attempt had broken the secret/non-secret config split. Resolved by having mcp/src/env.js load the root .env directly (reusing JIRA_API_TOKEN/CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN, no new secrets or env vars) while JIRA_URL/JIRA_EMAIL/CONFLUENCE_URL/spaceKey/projectKey continue to come from ripple.config.json via loadConfig(). .mcp.json stays secret-free, only declaring command/args/cwd.

skills/ripple/SKILL.md and mcp/mcp-config.json are canonical; per-host copies (.claude/skills, .agents/skills, .github/skills, .opencode/skills, .mcp.json, .agents/mcp_config.json) are generated by npm run sync:agents (scripts/sync-agents.mjs) since none of the target CLIs support includes/symlinks across arbitrary paths. Pattern mirrors github.com/santifer/career-ops (one router/instruction file, duplicated per-host, kept in sync by script). GitHub Copilot CLI needed no dedicated new target to function — it already reads .github/skills, .claude/skills, .agents/skills, and .mcp.json per its own docs, with .mcp.json taking precedence over ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json — but .github/skills/ripple/SKILL.md is synced anyway since it's Copilot's primary documented repo-level path. Confirmed Copilot CLI has no custom-slash-command primitive: /ripple works there purely because Ripple is wired as an auto-loaded/explicitly-invoked Skill.
MCP/Skill path has no raw LLM response to retry, so ripple__save_report validates the model's analysis JSON structurally instead of the v1 CLI's retry-once-then-throw behavior.
Originally logged as 'Claude is the default and only LLM implementation in v1.' Superseded — see the 2026-09-07 code-audit entry below: v1 now supports four providers.

src/llm/index.js's createLLM() now supports four providers, not just Claude: claude (Anthropic SDK, default model claude-sonnet-4-6), github (GitHub Models via src/llm/openai-compatible.js, default gpt-4o), openai (OpenAI-compatible, custom baseURL/apiKeyEnv), and ollama (local, defaults to http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1). runAnalyze() in src/commands/analyze.js validates the matching API key per provider (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / GITHUB_TOKEN / configurable env var) before calling the LLM.

bin/ripple.js exposes three commands, not two: init, analyze, and mcp-setup (src/commands/mcp-setup.js) — the last one was undocumented. mcp-setup runs `npm install --omit=dev` inside mcp/ and prints a ready-to-paste .mcp.json snippet plus host-restart instructions. analyze also supports --output both (markdown+json together), --verbose (dumps raw ticket/Confluence/test-suite data and the raw LLM response), and --no-llm (fetch-only mode: prints/saves a source dump, never calls an LLM) — none of these three flags were previously recorded.

src/utils/scrub.js's warnOnSecrets() flags likely credentials/tokens in ticket/wiki text before it reaches any LLM (used in both the v1 CLI and mcp/src/tools/get-ticket-context.js). src/utils/validate-url.js enforces HTTPS on custom LLM baseURLs (localhost exempted). src/sources/csv.js's loadTestSuite() confines the resolved CSV path to the project root. None of these were captured in prior feature/progress records.

log.topic: MCP scaffold state (supersedes stale security-auditor memory)
log.notes: The 2026-07-08 security-auditor memory ([[project_mcp_scaffold_state]]) described mcp/ as untracked in git, missing package.json, and having only 1 of 4 tools actually implemented (3 NOT_IMPLEMENTED stubs). As of this 2026-09-07 audit that state no longer holds: `git ls-files mcp` returns 13 tracked files including mcp/package.json (clean deps: only @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, dotenv, zod — no leftover express/hono in package.json, though the MCP SDK still pulls hono/express transitively for its optional HTTP transport, which Ripple does not use), and all four tools (get-ticket-context, get-release-context, aggregate-release-analysis, save-report) are fully implemented, not stubs.

The security-review finding in [[feedback_mcp_trust_boundary]] (a model-supplied testSuitePath confined only to the project root is too wide a trust boundary for MCP input) has been fixed: mcp/src/tools/get-ticket-context.js's resolveTestSuitePath() now requires the override to be a bare filename (no path separators) landing in the exact same directory as the operator-configured CSV, rejecting anything else with INVALID_INPUT.

CORRECTED 2026-09-07 by feature-record audit. This entry previously read that the Skill 'now instructs the model to prefer an active Atlassian Rovo connector's tools for ticket/Confluence fetching'. The actual text in skills/ripple/SKILL.md inverts that: ripple__get_ticket_context is called first and 'remains the default', and Rovo is offered as an option the model 'may prefer' for ticket/Confluence data only, with ripple__get_ticket_context still required for the CSV test-suite match Rovo cannot provide. The shipped behavior is correct; only the record was wrong.

Diffed the canonical sources against their generated targets: skills/ripple/SKILL.md is byte-identical to .claude/skills/ripple/SKILL.md, and mcp/mcp-config.json is byte-identical to .mcp.json. scripts/sync-agents.mjs matches its documented behavior. Also found .claude/commands/ripple.md, a dedicated custom slash command wrapping the Skill — not previously recorded anywhere.

Discovery uses three mechanisms in fixed precedence: explicit --pr/--commit/--compare, then the Jira dev-status Development panel (/rest/dev-status/1.0/issue/detail, which needs the ticket NUMERIC id, so fetchTicket now also returns `id`), then a GitHub search scoped to in:title,body preferring merged PRs. Local-git diffing was considered and explicitly ruled out of scope. Each tier falls through on a miss with a warning rather than throwing, so a missing diff degrades the analysis the same way missing Confluence context already does.

ripple__get_diff_context deliberately has NO repo parameter: the repository comes only from ripple.config.json. Architectural review caught that this alone was insufficient. The Jira dev-status panel is populated from ticket content, so anyone able to edit a ticket could plant a PR URL, steer the operator GitHub token at an arbitrary repo, and make the fetched diff a prompt-injection channel into a QA report. Fix: github.owner/repo (plus optional allowedRepos, validated at loadConfig as exactly two segments) act as an allowlist every ref is checked against, by exact case-insensitive match with no prefix matching, since a startsWith check would let acme-evil/x through an acme allowlist and a case-sensitive one would silently break the dev-status tier. A separate github.htmlBaseUrl (default https://github.com, NOT derivable from apiBaseUrl) validates the host: without it a planted gitlab.example/acme/storefront URL parses to an allowlisted owner/repo and Ripple fetches PR 1 from the real repo. parseRepoFromUrl output is only ever compared, never interpolated into a request URL.

log.topic: zod silently strips unknown keys (MCP schema)
log.notes: Confirmed empirically rather than assumed: the MCP SDK validateToolInput (mcp.js:180) returns parseResult.data, and a plain z.object() drops unknown keys at every nesting level, so codeChanges would have been silently deleted before any handler saw it. analysisShape had been duplicated verbatim in save-report.js and aggregate-release-analysis.js, so it was extracted to mcp/src/schemas/analysis.js AS A PURE NO-OP FIRST (identical shape, both tools importing it, tests green) and only then extended, making the non-breaking claim verifiable rather than asserted. The codeChanges shape is deliberately passthrough with all-optional fields: a type mismatch there throws McpError from inside the SDK request handler, outside the registerSafely try/catch, so the model would get an opaque protocol error with no error.fix. See issues.md.

skills/ripple/SKILL.md promises its template mirrors the v1 formatMarkdown byte for byte, so the new Code Changes section must not shift a single byte for reports without a diff. impactedTable already ends in a newline, so the only byte-preserving insertion is an interpolation at COLUMN 0 of the Recommended Tests line, empty-string in the no-diff case; every natural-looking alternative adds a newline. Enforced by golden fixtures generated from formatMarkdown BEFORE it was modified (regenerating them to make a failing test pass would defeat the point), plus the property formatMarkdown(a) === formatMarkdown with codeChanges undefined === formatMarkdown with codeChanges empty. The render condition is non-emptiness (must carry refs), not existence, because rule F sits in the prompt on every --diff run including runs where the diff failed.

log.topic: Code owns facts, model owns judgment
log.notes: filesChanged/additions/deletions/refs url values are facts fetchDiffContext knows exactly, so letting the LLM transcribe them would put model-authored PR links and diff stats into a QA artifact people act on. The model produces only modules and riskSignals, and the schema shown to it differs per path and says so explicitly. On the CLI, withCodeChanges() merges the real codeChangesFacts over the model output into a NEW object, never mutating the raw LLM response per the CLAUDE.md rule. On the MCP path save_report has no diff to re-derive from, so get_diff_context returns a ready-made codeChangesFacts block and SKILL.md instructs the model to copy it verbatim: structural enforcement on one surface, instructional on the other, with the difference stated rather than claimed as an absolute guarantee.

Caps are maxRefs 5, maxFiles 50, maxPatchChars 4000, with maxDiffChars 60000 as a budget ACROSS all refs, and across all tickets for ripple__get_release_context where the real hazard is context rather than round trips (30 tickets at 60000 chars is roughly 1.8MB in a single tool response); once spent, later tickets degrade to counts-only. includeDiff defaults to false on both context tools so existing callers see zero added GitHub traffic, asserted by a test that counts fetch calls by host. totals.filesChanged comes from the declared changed_files, never files.length, which is already truncated by the per_page=100 page size and would make omittedFiles wrong. Truncation is rendered as an explicit NOTE in buildUserPrompt text output, since the CLI model sees only that string and would otherwise treat a capped file list as complete.

Audited every claim in feature_list.json against the source rather than carrying it forward. Four claims were FALSE and were corrected: (1) '--release aggregated via aggregateReleaseAnalyses' — the release branch loops and prints one report per ticket and never aggregates; aggregateReleaseAnalyses is reached only from the multi---ticket path (analyze.js) and ripple__aggregate_release_analysis, and the release branch contained a dead 'if (!noLlm) {}' block where the aggregation was evidently intended. Now recorded accurately and tracked under knownGaps. (2) 'authGate gates every MCP tool on CONFLUENCE_API_TOKEN' — ripple__get_diff_context passes requireConfluence:false. (3) 'MCP tools: [four named]' — there are five since ripple__get_diff_context landed. (4) the Rovo entry inversion, corrected in place above. Five claims were understated and were widened to match the code: HTTPS enforcement covers Jira/Confluence/GitHub as well as LLM baseURLs; warnOnSecrets now also covers PR bodies and patch bodies on both surfaces; findRelevantTests also matches against the test description column; --verbose/--no-llm also carry the diff context. Five implemented features were absent from the records entirely and were added: RIPPLE_PROJECT_ROOT, the MCP success envelope's meta block, npm test / test:golden, the npm packaging whitelist, and the four .claude/agents subagents. One stale file reference was fixed: the deferred coverage-gap entry pointed at analysisShape inside save-report.js, which now lives in mcp/src/schemas/analysis.js.

log.topic: Code review fixes: false repo in codeChangesFacts
log.notes: Adversarial code review (BLOCKER CR-01) found fetchDiffContext hardcoding repo: `${owner}/${repo}` from the primary config in three places, including inside codeChangesFacts. github.allowedRepos exists precisely so a discovered ref can live in a sibling repo (monorepo split, fork); such a ref was fetched correctly from acme/mobile but reported as acme/storefront — a false value inside the one block whose entire purpose is carrying only values Ripple actually fetched, and which the model is told to copy verbatim. Fixed by deriving the repo from the refs that actually resolved (refMetas now carry owner/repo, deduped and joined), mirroring how aggregateCodeChanges already handles the multi-repo case. Regression test added; the gap existed because isRepoAllowed was only tested in isolation, never end-to-end through fetchDiffContext with an allowedRepos ref.

log.topic: Code review fixes: truncation flag conflated policy omission with size caps
log.notes: Adversarial code review (BLOCKER CR-02) found the deny-list branch setting truncated=true. Deny-listing removes neither a file from the list nor a byte from the diff budget — the file stays listed with real counts — so it must not flip the flag that drives 'the file list is NOT exhaustive'. Any PR touching a lockfile (i.e. any dependency bump) therefore produced 'showing 2 of 2 changed file(s) ... This file list is NOT exhaustive', a self-contradiction fed straight into the reasoning model and, per rule F, echoed into riskReason. Fixed by adding patchOmittedReason ('binary' | 'denylist' | 'budget'), leaving truncated set only for genuine size-cap loss, and splitting the single blanket NOTE into three accurate sentences gated on their own conditions. The existing test missed this because it always paired the deny-listed file with a genuinely oversized patch, making truncated=true correct for an unrelated reason.

log.topic: Code review fixes: warnings WR-01 through WR-06
log.notes: WR-01: commit SHAs from GitHub search were the one ref-producing path with no format validation, breaking the stated invariant that search results are no more trusted than dev-status entries — now checked against SHA_PATTERN. WR-02: removed an unreachable 'res.status === 429' test inside the 401/403 branch. WR-03: --pr/--commit/--compare are now mutually exclusive; previously passing two silently merged unrelated changes into one codeChangesFacts. WR-04: diffCharBudget relaxed from positive() to nonnegative(), since get_release_context legitimately passes 0 once the release budget is spent (it worked only because that internal call bypasses SDK validation). WR-05: codeChangesFacts now carries truncated/omittedFiles, so a saved report cannot look like a complete diff when the model skips the rule-F instruction to mention truncation in prose. WR-06: the ticket/wiki warnOnSecrets calls sat BELOW the --no-llm early return, so fetch-only mode never scanned ticket or wiki text for credentials even though it prints that content and writes it to a -sources.txt file; moved above the return to match the diff scrub. IN-01: removed the dead 'if (!noLlm) {}' block in the release branch, replacing it with a comment pointing at the knownGaps entry. Suite is 59 tests, all passing.

log.topic: KAN-14: cap PR/commit body text in diff context
log.notes: PR/commit description text was the one piece of fetched content fetchDiffContext did not bound: bodies[] took payload.meta.body as-is at any size, charging nothing against maxDiffChars. Worst on the MCP path, where ripple__get_diff_context returns the whole diffContext (bodies included) into the host model's context. Fixed with github.maxBodyChars (default 4000, mirroring maxPatchChars), clamped with Math.max(0, ...) before use because slice(0, -100) means 'all but the last 100 chars' — a negative config value would invert the field rather than merely skip the cap — and a cap of 0 now omits the body instead of pushing an empty string. Two decisions worth keeping. (1) A cut body does NOT set the global truncated flag. That flag means diff content was withheld: formatSourceDump renders it as 'showing N of M file(s)' and SKILL.md rule F turns it into an instruction to distrust the file list, so on a complete two-file PR with a long description reusing it would print 'Truncated: showing 2 of 2 file(s)' and put a false claim into riskReason. It is the same conflation the comments at github.js:626-638 already guard against for deny-listed patches, so body truncation became a fourth distinct condition with its own counter (totals.truncatedBodies and codeChangesFacts.truncatedBodies) plus a warnings[] entry, which is the only thing that makes the cut visible on the CLI at all — bodies appear in neither the prompt nor the source dump, so without the warning the truncation would surface only under --output json. KAN-14's AC allowed this explicitly ('truncated and/or a new field'). (2) maxBodyChars is a PER-REF cap: it bounds one description and says nothing about how many arrive together, so the aggregate across a release is bounded separately, in ripple__get_release_context. Same config number, two jobs: in github.js maxDiffChars is a patch budget feeding the prompt, where spending it on prose the prompt never includes is a pure loss, so bodies are not charged against remainingChars there; in get-release-context.js it is a total-bytes guard on one response carrying every ticket's bodies verbatim, so after each ticket's patches are charged, its bodies are handed only the room left and get nothing at all once the budget is spent (a warning naming github.maxDiffChars goes into that ticket's diffContext.warnings). Release-level trimming is deliberately not folded into totals.truncatedBodies, which records only what the per-ref cap did. Correction worth recording: the architect review found the release-path hole, but the first fix for it only added body lengths into the spent subtraction, which made the bookkeeping honest and enforced nothing — remainingBudget is forwarded as diffCharBudget, which gates patches only (remainingChars in github.js), and fetchDiffContext never consults a budget before pushing a body, so 30 tickets x 5 refs x 4000 chars = 600,000 chars was still reachable. Code review caught that the code comment, issues.md and this log all overstated that as a closed hole; the aggregate trimming above is what actually enforces the bound, and it lives in get-release-context.js rather than as a skipBodies flag threaded into fetchDiffContext so the per-run path keeps its patch-budget semantics unchanged. tests/get-release-context.test.js now pins the bound (it fails against the charging-only version). Both sites are commented so neither gets 'fixed' into the other. Accepted residual: warnOnSecrets now scans the capped body, so a credential past char 4000 of a PR description no longer warns. Not an exposure regression — that warning is about content 'that will be sent to the LLM', and text past the cap never is. Cap-before-scan is forced anyway: github.js:6-9 forbids the module from printing, so it cannot call warnOnSecrets itself, and returning the uncapped body to consumers would defeat the cap. Markdown output is byte-identical (renderCodeChanges renders no truncation field); the new field appears only in JSON. No schema edit needed — codeChangesShape is .passthrough(). SKILL.md's codeChangesFacts field list was also drifting (it omitted truncated and omittedFiles too) and now names all three counters, re-synced to the four host copies via npm run sync:agents. Suite is 65 tests, all passing (three new release-budget cases in tests/get-release-context.test.js).
